Chapter One: Childhood in a World of Rules and Expectations
Imagine growing up in a place where every move matters—a home in early twentieth-century Paris, where expectations are woven into the very fabric of daily life.
For one little girl, that was just reality. She breathed in the hopes and worries of a middle-class family, where tradition and reputation weren’t just important—they were everything. There was an unspoken belief that a daughter’s actions reflected directly on her parents, especially her mother, who clung tightly to the rituals and values she’d learned as a child herself.
Mornings set the tone. There was careful grooming, the right clothes, and a sense that someone was always watching. Her mother hovered—sometimes with warmth, sometimes with anxiety—constantly shaping, correcting, and nudging her daughter to be the very picture of good behavior. Her father, once full of promise, now carried the weight of disappointment. His dreams for his daughter were colored by his own regrets.
In this kind of environment, love and approval felt closely tied to obedience. The girl learned to read the room, adjusting her words and actions to whatever the adults expected. Sure, there was comfort in making her parents proud, but underneath, she began to feel uneasy—almost as if she had to tuck away who she really was.
School wasn’t much of an escape. The rules followed her there, too. Teachers demanded discipline. Classmates competed for praise. The message was clear: if you wanted to succeed, you had to fit in, not stand out. But beneath that, a quiet curiosity started to grow. Books became her secret hideout—a place where she could explore new ideas without anyone’s judgment.
As the years went by, the boundaries set by home and school started to feel a bit tight—almost suffocating. She noticed how her world wasn’t quite like everyone else’s. Some kids had more freedom, others even less. Watching her mother run the household, always careful, always trying to look just right, she realized that being a daughter meant carrying not just love, but the full weight of her family’s hopes and fears.
Of course, it wasn’t all strictness and rules. There were bright moments—holidays, little wins at school, the warm hug of a parent. But even then, the happiness seemed to come with strings attached. Being good felt like the safest way to be, and safety meant following the rules.
Over time, questions started bubbling up. Why did her brother get more freedom? Why were some things never talked about? Why was her mother always so anxious, so determined to keep every detail under control? These quiet questions slowly shaped how she saw herself.
And then, the first little cracks appeared. She realized her parents’ values didn’t always match how she felt inside. Part of her longed to please them—of course—but another part wanted to figure out the world for herself. That tug-of-war between loyalty and independence became a constant, setting the stage for everything that would come next.
So, in these early years, the seeds of change were quietly planted. Not with grand gestures or loud rebellion, but in those small moments of doubt and curiosity. That’s where her journey of self-discovery truly began—even if no one noticed it at the time.
